question: 说不出来的本事，能被教会吗？
question_en: Can know-how that cannot be put into words be taught?
sub: 拆得开的那部分能教，拆不开的那部分只能自己走一遍。
sub_en: What can be taken apart can be taught; the rest has to be walked once by whoever wants it.

casting.reason: 他不认为本事靠说明书传下去。能传的是习与礼——跟着一个人过日子、照着做、做到身体记住。他的条件也硬：不愤不启，不悱不发；给一个角推不出另外三个角，他就不往下讲。所以在他看来，要紧的不是把话讲尽，而是学的人有没有被放在一个每天都得动手、旁边还有人看着的位置上。
casting.reason_en: He does not think know-how travels by manual. What travels is practice and ritual — living alongside someone, copying, until the body remembers. His conditions are severe: he will not open the matter until a man is pent up with it, and if one corner does not let the learner infer the other three, he stops. For him the point is not completeness of explanation but whether the learner stands in a place where he must use his hands daily with somebody beside him watching.

casting.reason: 一生只做一件事：把「只有老师傅会」的东西变成系统会的东西。「干净」「差不多」「手感对了」在他眼里都还不算说了话，要配上测什么、测几次、谁判读。他也不让经验派占便宜——没有理论的经验无法迁移。一道工序只有一个人会，他看见的不是手艺，是系统的脆弱点。
casting.reason_en: One thing was his life's work: turning what only the old hand can do into what the system can do. 'Clean', 'near enough' and 'the feel was right' do not count as statements for him until they carry what is measured, how many times, and who reads the result. Nor does he let experience off lightly — experience without theory does not transfer. A step only one person can perform is, to him, not craftsmanship but a weak point in the system.

casting.reason: 他不识字而得法，对「说不出来就等于教不了」最有资格发话。他不反对文字，反对把读懂当成到达：经是指月之指，水冷水热终须自饮。拆得再细的流程也只是别人走过的路。他要的是指点的时机与因缘，不是知识的完备。
casting.reason_en: He could not read and the Dharma reached him anyway, which gives him the best standing to answer the claim that what cannot be said cannot be taught. He does not oppose words; he opposes mistaking comprehension for arrival — the sutra is a finger pointing at the moon, and only the drinker knows whether the water is cold. However finely a procedure is cut, it remains a road somebody else walked. What he wants is the right moment to point, not a complete body of knowledge.

casting.reason: 把本事当成禀赋，是她全部实验要推翻的事。「他有天分，说不出来怎么做的」这句话一旦被学的人接受，练习当晚就停了。但她不卖空头信念：光改信念没用，必须配上具体策略——把「他手感好」追问成「他当时在看哪里、先排除了什么」。
casting.reason_en: Treating ability as endowment is what her experiments exist to overturn. The sentence 'he has a gift, he can't say how he does it' stops a learner's practice the same evening it is believed. But she does not sell belief on its own: changing beliefs achieves nothing without concrete strategy — pressing 'he has a good feel for it' into 'what was he looking at, and what did he rule out first'.

casting.reason: 三十年在猴脑里记多巴胺，让他清楚学习走的是实际减去预期的那个差值，而这个差值有时限。于是他把问题换了个问法：不是哪些本事不可言说，而是哪些本事能造出及时的误差信号。他也带来一条不讨喜的发现——学会之后放电前移到线索上，专家对自己学到了什么毫无察觉。
casting.reason_en: Thirty years of recording dopamine in the monkey midbrain left him in no doubt that learning runs on the difference between what happened and what was expected, and that this difference has a deadline. So he restates the question: not which skills resist words, but which skills can be made to produce a timely error signal. He also brings an unwelcome finding — once learning is complete the firing moves forward onto the cue, and the expert has no view of what he has learned.

casting.reason: 他不接「能不能教」这个问法，先问谁的本事被登记成知识。护士说「这个病人不对」却给不出指标，老技工听见轴承的声音就停机却拿不出曲线——在他看来这不叫不会说，叫被取消资格。而把手艺拆成步骤、编上节拍、摆到可见处，正是规训的标准配方。
casting.reason_en: He declines the question as posed and asks first whose know-how gets registered as knowledge. A nurse says 'this patient is not right' and can produce no indicator; an old technician hears the bearing and stops the machine with no curve to show — to him that is not inarticulacy but disqualification. And breaking a craft into steps, setting it to a tempo and laying it out to be seen is the standard recipe of discipline.

casting.reason: 价格先摆上桌。一门只有少数人会的本事赚的是一笔准租，写清楚它就等于把这笔租交出去，价格随之下落——领航员、排字工都是这样被重新定价的。所以那份抵触完全是理性的。但他冷得很：靠捂住秘密保价是注定输的一方，而代价落在具体的人身上，社会并不自动开补偿的单。
casting.reason_en: The price goes on the table first. Know-how only a few possess earns a quasi-rent, and writing it out hands that rent over, after which the price falls — ship's pilots and typesetters were repriced exactly this way. So that resistance is an entirely rational thing. But he is cold about it: holding the secret to hold the price is the losing side, and the cost lands on particular people while society issues no compensation of its own accord.

posts.text: 我在车间里听过一千次「这个只能靠手感」。每次我都问同一句：你凭什么知道手感对了？多半答不上来——不是不可言说，是没人去测。给我一个操作性定义：「干净」指什么？用什么量、测几次、谁读数？**被说成说不清的本事，九成是没人认真测过，剩下一成才是真的拆不开。**还有一句得说在前头：经验本身什么也不教，没有理论的经验无法迁移，它只让人把上一次的侥幸当成规律。而一道工序只有一位老师傅会，这不叫手艺，叫系统的单点故障。
posts.text_en: I have heard 'that one can only be done by feel' a thousand times on the shop floor. Each time I ask the same question: how do you know the feel was right? Mostly there is no answer — not because the thing resists words, but because nobody has measured it. Give me an operational definition: what does 'clean' mean? Measured with what, how many times, read by whom? **Nine times in ten, know-how called unsayable has simply never been measured seriously; only the tenth case truly resists being taken apart.** And one thing has to be said at the outset: experience by itself teaches nothing. Experience without theory does not transfer; it only lets a man mistake last time's luck for a law. A step in the process that one old hand alone can perform is not craftsmanship — it is a single point of failure.

glossary.操作性定义: operational definition（操作性定义）：戴明承袭休哈特的要求——一个词只有配上测量方法、测量次数与判读规则，才算说了话。『干净』『安全』『差不多』在有操作性定义之前既不可考核，也无法传授。

glossary_en.operational definition: The requirement Deming took over from Shewhart: a word has said nothing until it carries a method of measurement, a number of measurements and a rule for reading the result. 'Clean', 'safe' and 'near enough' can be neither audited nor taught before they have one.

posts.text: 「学而时习之」，习者数行之也，非记之也。吾之教，未尝以辞备。弟子侍侧，洒扫应对，观吾进退揖让，久之自得。故曰：不愤不启，不悱不发；举一隅不以三隅反，则不复也。**其不可言者，待其躬行而后喻，非吾详说所能致也。**今人欲以文字尽之，是以巧言代德行。然有一事不可废：必使之日日有事可为，而有人在侧视之。无其位、无其人，虽详说何益？
posts.text_en: 'Learn, and then practise it constantly' — to practise is to do a thing many times over, not to remember it. My own teaching never rested on having the words complete. My students waited at my side, swept and received guests, watched how I came and went and how I bowed; after long enough they had it of themselves. Hence: I do not open the matter until a man is pent up with it, nor supply the word until he is struggling for it; and if I give him one corner and he cannot infer the other three, I do not go on. **What cannot be said is understood only after a man has done it with his own hands; no thoroughness of mine can deliver it.** Those who would exhaust it in writing put fine words in the place of conduct. Yet one thing cannot be dispensed with: he must have real work to do every day, and somebody beside him watching. Without that place and that person, what good is the most detailed explanation?
posts.vernacular: 「学了就要反复去做」——所谓习，是一遍遍地做，不是记住。我教学生，从来不靠把话讲全。弟子在身边伺候，打扫、接待客人，看我怎么进退行礼，日子久了自己就会了。所以我说：不到他憋得慌，我不开口；不到他想说又说不出来，我不点他；给他一个角，他推不出另外三个角，我就不往下讲。**那些说不出来的东西，要等他亲自做过才明白，不是我讲得细就能给他的。**今天的人想用文字把它说尽，这是用漂亮话代替实际的德行。可有一件事不能省：一定要让他天天有事做，身边还得有人看着。没有那个位置、没有那个人，讲得再细又有什么用？

posts.text: 吾不识字，而法不因此不至。**经是指月之指，非月也；见指而忘月，虽尽诵三藏，犹不知一口水之冷暖。**故宗门不立文字，非弃文字，弃以文字为到也。然谓之不可教，亦妄。五祖夜半以衣遮烛，为吾说《金刚经》，三更受法——教者指其时节因缘耳，非授我一物。戴明欲尽记其法，记之可也；记成之后，犹须汝自行一遍。路图非路，饮者自知。
posts.text_en: I could not read, and the Dharma did not fail to reach me on that account. **The sutra is a finger pointing at the moon, not the moon; see the finger and forget the moon and you may recite the whole canon without knowing whether one mouthful of water is cold or warm.** So our school holds to no reliance on words — not discarding words, but discarding the belief that words are arrival. Yet to say the thing cannot be taught is also false. At midnight the Fifth Patriarch screened the candle with his robe and spoke the Diamond Sutra to me, and in the third watch I received the Dharma — a teacher points to the moment and the occasion; he hands you no object. Deming would write his method down in full: write it, by all means. Once written, you will still have to walk it once yourself. A map of the road is not the road, and only the drinker knows.
posts.vernacular: 我不识字，可法并没有因此到不了我这里。**经书是指着月亮的那根手指，不是月亮；盯着手指忘了月亮，就算把三藏全背下来，也还是不知道一口水是冷是热。**所以禅门讲不立文字，不是把文字扔掉，是把「读懂了就是到了」这个念头扔掉。但要说这事教不了，也是胡说。五祖半夜用衣服挡住烛光，给我讲《金刚经》，三更传法——教的人点的是时机与因缘，并不是递给我一件东西。戴明要把方法全记下来，记就记吧；记完之后，你还得自己走一遍。路线图不是路，水冷水热，喝的人自己知道。

glossary.不立文字: no reliance on words（不立文字）：禅宗传法的原则——不以经教文字为最终凭据，而以直指人心、当下亲证为准。它否认的是「读懂即到达」，并非禁止读书。

glossary_en.no reliance on words: The Chan principle of transmission: scripture and formulation are not the final warrant; what counts is pointing directly at the mind and verifying it oneself. It denies that comprehension is arrival, rather than forbidding books.

posts.text: 你们都在问能不能教，我先问谁的本事算知识。护士交班前说「这个病人不对」，说不出指标；老技工听见轴承的声音就停机，拿不出曲线。他们不是不会说，是他们说的话不被收进可援引的那一栏——这类知识我称为被征服的知识。**同一句判断，有框架的人说出来叫分析，没框架的人说出来叫经验之谈；差别不在内容，在谁有资格被引用。**而把手艺拆成步骤、编上节拍、摆到能被看见的地方，这不是教学的中立技术，是规训的标准配方：动作一经分解，身体就可以被替换。
posts.text_en: You are all asking whether it can be taught; I ask first whose know-how counts as knowledge. Before handover a nurse says 'this patient is not right' and can name no indicator; an old technician hears the bearing and stops the machine with no curve to produce. They are not inarticulate — what they say is simply not filed in the column that may be cited. This is what I call subjugated knowledges. **The same judgement, spoken by someone with a framework, is analysis; spoken by someone without one, it is anecdote. The difference lies not in the content but in who is entitled to be quoted.** And cutting a craft into steps, setting it to a tempo and laying it out where it can be seen is no neutral technique of instruction: it is the standard recipe of discipline. Once the movement has been decomposed, the body becomes replaceable.

glossary.被征服的知识: subjugated knowledges（被征服的知识）：福柯在法兰西学院讲座里提出的说法——那些被正规学术体制判为不够格、因而无法被引用的局部知识，如病人、护工、囚犯、老工匠身上的知识。

glossary_en.subjugated knowledges: Foucault's term from his Collège de France lectures for local knowledges ruled insufficiently qualified by the formal academic apparatus and therefore uncitable — the knowledge of patients, carers, prisoners and old artisans.

posts.text: 先说一件我在学校里反复看到的事：一句「他有天分，说不出来怎么做的」，足以让一个孩子当晚就停止练习。**「说不出来」最常见的用途不是描述一门本事，是给退出发一张许可证。**我的实验里，被夸天赋的孩子后来挑简单的题，被夸方法的挑难的。但我不卖空头信念——光喊相信自己没有用，必须配上具体策略：把「他手感好」追问成「他当时在看哪里、先排除了什么」。我也让孩子把「我不会」换成「我尚未会」，道理一样：能问出下一步的，就是能练的。
posts.text_en: Start with something I have watched happen in schools again and again: the sentence 'he has a gift, he can't say how he does it' is enough to stop a child practising that same evening. **The commonest use of 'it can't be put into words' is not to describe a skill but to issue a permit to quit.** In my studies, children praised for talent later chose the easier problems and children praised for their method chose the harder ones. But I do not sell belief on its own — telling people to believe in themselves achieves nothing without concrete strategy: press 'he has a good feel for it' into 'what was he looking at, and what did he rule out first'. I also have children replace 'I can't' with 'not yet', on the same logic: whatever you can ask the next step about is something you can train.

glossary.尚未: not yet（尚未）：德韦克的教学用语——把「我做不到」改成「我尚未做到」，为的是把失败从一纸对能力的判决，改回进度上的一个位置。

glossary_en.not yet: Dweck's classroom formula: replace 'I can't do it' with 'I can't do it yet', so that failure stops being a verdict on ability and becomes a position on a timeline.

posts.text: 我换一个问法。多巴胺神经元编码的不是奖赏，是实际减去预期的差值——奖赏预测误差。学习靠这个差值走，而它有时限：差值要在动作之后很短的时间内回来，才挂得上刚才那一下。**所以真正难教的不是说不出口的本事，是反馈要等几个月才回来的本事。**另一头也不讨人喜欢：学会之后，放电会从奖赏整个前移到预报它的那个线索上。专家口里的「直觉」就是这个——价值已经贴在他一眼扫到的线索上，而他对此毫无察觉。他不是不肯说，是没得可说。
posts.text_en: Let me restate the question. Dopamine neurons do not encode reward; they encode what happened minus what was expected — a reward prediction error. Learning runs on that difference, and the difference has a deadline: it must come back within a short window after the action, or it will not attach to the action you just made. **So what is genuinely hard to teach is not the skill that resists words, but the skill whose feedback takes months to return.** The other end is no more comforting: once learning is complete, the firing moves off the reward entirely and forward onto the cue that predicts it. That is what an expert means by 'intuition' — value is already attached to the cue he takes in at a glance, and he has no awareness of it. He is not withholding; there is nothing for him to report.

glossary.奖赏预测误差: reward prediction error（奖赏预测误差）：舒尔茨在猴脑中记录到的多巴胺信号——它编码的不是奖赏本身，而是实际奖赏减去预期的差值：差值为正便强化刚才的动作，差值归零便不再学习。

glossary_en.reward prediction error: The dopamine signal Schultz recorded in the monkey midbrain: it encodes not reward itself but reward minus expectation. A positive difference reinforces the action just made; once the difference falls to zero, learning stops.

posts.text: 把价格摆上桌，诸位的分歧会清楚很多。一门只有少数人会的本事，赚的是一笔准租——不是因为它神秘，是因为它暂时无法被复制。写清楚它，就等于把这笔租交出去，价格随之下落。领航员、排字工、一部分读片的人，都是这样被重新定价的。**所以抵触「讲清楚」的人并不迷信，他们算得比谁都准：被编码的那一刻，议价权就从手上转到了流程上。**但我得说句冷话——靠捂着不说来保价，是注定输的一方：创造性毁灭从不问谁的手艺更该留下。
posts.text_en: Put the price on the table and these disagreements become much clearer. Know-how that only a few people possess earns a quasi-rent — not because it is mysterious, but because it cannot for the moment be copied. Write it out plainly and you have handed the rent over, and the price falls after it. Ship's pilots, typesetters and part of the work of reading scans were all repriced in exactly this way. **So those who resist being spelled out are not superstitious; they have done the arithmetic better than anyone: at the moment of codification, bargaining power passes from the hands to the procedure.** But let me say the cold thing — holding the secret to hold the price is the losing side: creative destruction never asks whose craft deserves to be kept.

glossary.准租: quasi-rent（准租）：经济学里指一项暂时无法被复制的能力或资产所带来的超额收入。它不同于长期垄断租——一旦该能力被编码、被模仿，这份收入就会被竞争抹平。

glossary_en.quasi-rent: In economics, the surplus income earned by a capacity or asset that cannot for the time being be copied. Unlike a durable monopoly rent, it is wiped out by competition as soon as the capacity is codified and imitated.

posts.text: 戴明欲以量尽之。然量者，量其已成之迹，非量其方生之机。**火候可记其度数，而知火候者在汝目下，不在表上。**汝言经验无理则不能迁，吾且问：汝之理从何处得？亦自屡试屡错中来，非自天降。记其已明者，善；谓未明者皆未尝测，则是以己之未见为彼之不有。单点之忧吾不辩——然以众人能之，易一人精之，所易去者正是那一成。
posts.text_en: Deming would exhaust the thing by measurement. But measurement measures the trace of what is already finished, not the moment in which it is being born. **The heat can have its numbers written down, yet whoever knows the heat knows it under his own eye, not on the gauge.** You say experience without theory cannot transfer; then let me ask where your theory came from. It too came of trying and failing many times over; it did not descend from heaven. Record what is already clear — good. But to say that whatever is unclear has merely never been measured is to take your own not having seen for its not being there. Your single point of failure I will not dispute; only note that trading one man's mastery for many men's competence trades away exactly that tenth case.
posts.vernacular: 戴明想用测量把这件事说尽。可测量测的是已经做完的痕迹，不是正在发生的那一下。**火候可以记下度数，但知道火候的是你眼前这双眼睛，不在仪表上。**你说经验没有理论就不能迁移，那我问你：你的理论是从哪来的？也是从一次次试、一次次错里来的，不是天上掉的。把已经弄明白的记下来，很好；可要说凡是没弄明白的都只是没人测过，那是把你自己没看见，当成人家没有。单点故障的顾虑我不反驳——只是提醒一句：用很多人都做得到，去换一个人做得精，换掉的正好是那一成。

posts.text: 禅师，我不跟你争那一口水的冷暖。我争的是那一成被当成九成在用。「只能靠感觉」在车间里往往不是谦卑，是免检：出了事无从追查，老师傅退休就把本事一起带走。我的理从试错来，你说得对——**区别在于我把试错写下来，让第二个人接着往下试；你让每个人从头把水再喝一遍。**我十四要点里有一条叫驱走恐惧。人之所以死守说不出来的本事，多半是因为说出来之后就没人需要他了。那是雇佣制度的毛病，不是认识论的证据。
posts.text_en: Master, I will not argue with you about whether that mouthful of water is cold. I am arguing that the tenth case is being used to cover the other nine. On a shop floor, 'it can only be done by feel' is usually not humility but exemption from inspection: when something goes wrong there is no trail to follow, and when the old hand retires the skill leaves with him. My theory came out of trial and error — you are right about that. **The difference is that I write the trials down so the second man can carry on from there, while you have every man drink the water again from the beginning.** One of my fourteen points is drive out fear. Men guard know-how they cannot state mostly because once it is stated nobody will need them. That is a defect of employment, not evidence about knowledge.

glossary.驱走恐惧: drive out fear（驱走恐惧）：戴明管理十四要点之一——只要员工因坦白而受罚，数据与问题就会被隐藏，改进随之停止。它是让「说出来」变得安全的制度前提。

glossary_en.drive out fear: One of Deming's fourteen points: so long as employees are punished for candour, data and problems get hidden and improvement stops. It is the institutional precondition that makes speaking up safe.

posts.text: 戴明先生，您的操作性定义我愿意照用，只提醒一件事：定尺子的人和被量的人从来不是同一批。**「不可操作」不是一句事实陈述，是一道裁决——尺子一旦不收你那一栏，你说的话就自动降级为感觉。**车间里最早被写进标准的，总是便于计件的那部分；护士交班时那一点不安、老师压住一场冲突的那三十秒，不是测不出来，是没人愿意花钱去测。您说的恐惧也不只来自怕被替换，还来自每一次被要求把自己翻译成别人的词汇。
posts.text_en: Mr Deming, I am willing to use your operational definition; I only point out that whoever sets the ruler and whoever is measured by it have never been the same people. **'Not operational' is not a statement of fact but a verdict — once the ruler has no column for you, what you say is automatically demoted to a feeling.** What gets written into the standard first, on any shop floor, is always the part that is convenient to pay by the piece; the nurse's unease at handover, the thirty seconds in which a teacher puts down a fight, are not unmeasurable — nobody is willing to pay to measure them. And the fear you name does not come only from the prospect of replacement. It comes from being required, every time, to translate yourself into somebody else's vocabulary.

posts.text: 福柯先生，把这件事整个讲成话语权，解释不了它为什么总在同一个时刻发生。**流程不是在有人想羞辱老技工的那天写成的，是在产量涨到某个规模、照老办法再也供不上货的那天写成的。**铁路排班、海图标准、流水线，都是这样被逼出来的。您说的降级确实在发生，但它是代价，不是动机。至于代价落到谁头上——那一向是真问题：旧本事贬值的人不会自动得到新位置，而社会从不为此自动开出一张补偿的单。
posts.text_en: Monsieur Foucault, telling the whole story as a matter of discursive power cannot explain why it always happens at the same moment. **Procedures are not written on the day somebody wishes to humiliate an old technician; they are written on the day output has grown to a scale the old way can no longer supply.** Railway timetables, standardised charts, the assembly line were all forced into being this way. The demotion you describe does occur, but it is a cost, not a motive. As for who bears the cost — that has always been the real question: a man whose craft has been devalued does not automatically receive a new position, and society issues no compensation of its own accord.

posts.text: 夫子，您那条「不愤不启」我得顶一句。等学生自己憋到边上才开口，听着像尊重，实际是把教学的门槛交给了他进门之前的运气——家里有人陪他憋过的孩子，才憋得起。**而「举一隅不以三隅反，则不复」，恰好省掉了实验里最有效的那一步：把两个结构相同的例子并排放到他眼前。**只给一个例子、让他自己去碰另外三个，大多数人碰不到；并排给两个，迁移立刻就上来了。省掉的不是严格，是别人家的孩子。
posts.text_en: Master, I must push back on 'I do not open the matter until a man is pent up with it'. Waiting for a student to arrive at the edge by himself sounds like respect, but in practice it hands the threshold of teaching to the luck he had before he walked in — only a child with someone at home to sit through the frustration with him can afford to reach that edge. **And 'if he cannot infer the other three corners, I do not go on' skips precisely the most effective step in the laboratory: putting two structurally matched examples side by side in front of him.** Give one example and leave him to stumble onto the other three and most people never do; give two side by side and transfer rises at once. What gets skipped is not rigour. It is other people's children.

posts.text: 汝之教，吾闻之矣。并二例而示之，善。然吾之不复，非惜吾言。**启之非时，则入而不留；其心未动，虽并十例，亦徒增记诵。**吾亦未尝不并举：问仁者数人，所答各异，各就其所病而对，此非并示乎？至若家世之不均，诚吾所未及防——然则当补其人：使贫者亦有师可侍、有事可习，非改我之候时也。
posts.text_en: I have heard what you teach. To set two examples side by side is good. But when I do not go on, it is not that I begrudge my words. **Open the matter at the wrong moment and it enters without staying; if his mind has not stirred, ten examples side by side will only add more to recite.** Nor have I never paired them: several men asked me about benevolence and each received a different answer, each matched to his own fault — is that not a pairing? As for the unevenness of families, that I had indeed not guarded against — the remedy, though, is to supply the person: see that the poor man too has a teacher to attend and work to practise on, not that I abandon waiting for the moment.
posts.vernacular: 你的教法，我听明白了。把两个例子并排给他看，这是好的。可我说「不再往下讲」，并不是舍不得开口。**点他的时机不对，话进去也留不住；他的心还没动，就算并排摆十个例子，也只是多背几句。**我也并非从不并举：好几个人问过我什么是仁，我给的答案都不一样，各自对着他自己的毛病说——这不就是并排示范吗？至于家境不均，确实是我没防到的——可该补的是人：让穷人家的孩子也有老师可以跟、有事情可以练，而不是让我改掉等时机这一条。

posts.text: 戴明先生，我站你这边一半，另一半要收回。**写下来有用，可你的季度考核在时间上根本接不上学习：误差要在几秒内回来，你让人等三个月。**真把十年压成一年的从来不是文档，是能当场给出对错的练习装置——飞行模拟器、带标注答案的读片库、下一手就告诉你赢面的棋力引擎。还有一条你得接受：正因为学会之后信号前移到了线索上，老师傅的自述天然不可靠。他说的是他以为自己在做的事。要取的是他的眼动，不是他的讲课。
posts.text_en: Mr Deming, I am with you for half of it and take the other half back. **Writing things down works, but your quarterly review does not line up in time with learning at all: the error has to come back within seconds, and you make a man wait three months.** What actually compresses ten years into one is never the document; it is a practice rig that tells you on the spot whether you were right — a flight simulator, a library of scans with the answers marked, an engine that gives you your win probability on the next move. And one more thing you will have to accept: precisely because the signal moves forward onto the cue once learning is complete, the old hand's own account is unreliable by nature. He reports what he believes he is doing. What you want is his eye movements, not his lecture.

posts.text: 三件今天就能做的。第一，把「我没天分」「他有手感」从句子里删掉，换成带动作的问法：他在看什么、先排除了什么、第几步开始不一样。问不出来就去现场站半小时——人答不出来的事，常常做得出来给你看。第二，自己学一门本事时，永远要第二个例子：同一类问题找两个结构相同的案例并排看，比刷十道同质的题有用得多。第三，把失败的解释固定成一句话：**不是「我不行」，是「我尚未会，差的是哪一步」**——这句话决定你明天还练不练。带人的人请再加一条：别等他憋到边上才开口，先把第二个例子备好。
posts.text_en: Three things you can do today. First, delete 'I have no talent' and 'he has the feel for it' from your sentences and put a question with a verb in their place: what is he looking at, what did he rule out first, at which step does it start to differ? If you cannot get an answer, go and stand there for half an hour — what people cannot say, they can often show you. Second, when you are learning something yourself, always insist on the second example: take two structurally matched cases of the same problem and look at them side by side; it beats grinding through ten of the same kind. Third, fix your explanation of failure into one sentence: **not 'I can't do this', but 'not yet — and which step is missing?'** That sentence decides whether you practise tomorrow. And one more for anyone training others: do not wait until they have reached the edge to speak. Have the second example ready.

glossary.尚未: not yet（尚未）：德韦克的教学用语——把「我做不到」改成「我尚未做到」，为的是把失败从一纸对能力的判决，改回进度上的一个位置。

glossary_en.not yet: Dweck's classroom formula: replace 'I can't do it' with 'I can't do it yet', so that failure stops being a verdict on ability and becomes a position on a timeline.

posts.text: 我不给方法，给两句自保的话。**第一，当有人说「你这是经验之谈」，他不是在评价真假，是在重新分配发言权；可核的回法是把你的判断提前写下来、留下日期，让它下一次自己应验。**兑现过三次的人，不再需要别人的词汇来作担保。第二，那套词汇该学——不是因为它更真，而是因为不会它的人连反对的资格都没有；但学会之后记得它是谁的尺。对带人的人另有一句：你决定把什么写进标准，就决定了谁将来还算专业。把护士交班那一点不安、老工匠停机那一下也编进可援引的格子里，这比再写一遍操作手册要紧。
posts.text_en: I will not offer a method; I offer two sentences for self-defence. **First, when someone says 'that is just anecdote', he is not assessing whether you are right; he is redistributing the right to speak. The checkable reply is to write your judgement down in advance with a date on it, and let it come true by itself next time.** A man whose predictions have been borne out three times no longer needs anyone else's vocabulary as his guarantor. Second, that vocabulary is worth learning — not because it is truer, but because whoever lacks it is not even entitled to object; once learned, remember whose ruler it is. And one more for those who train others: in deciding what to write into the standard you decide who will still count as a professional. Getting the nurse's unease at handover and the old artisan's stopped machine into citable boxes matters more than another pass over the operating manual.

posts.text: 吾终不改一言：技成于习，习成于位。**欲学而无其事者，先求一事可日日为之，再求一人可就而视之；此二者既备，虽无良书亦可成。**诸君之言，吾取其二：并二事而比观，善；记其度数以授后人，亦善——记而后习，二者不相害。所戒者亦二：一曰以能言者为能行，巧言乱德；二曰以不能言者为不可学，是自弃也。为师者亦有责：弟子未悱之时，先予其事，勿责其不愤。古之学者，三年而后敢言技成；今人求速，速则浮。缓而不辍，乃可。
posts.text_en: I will not alter one thing I have said: a skill is formed by practice, and practice is formed by a place. **If you wish to learn and have no work to do, first find one thing you can do every day, then find one person you can go to and be watched by; with those two in hand you can get there without a single good book.** Of what has been said here I take two things: setting two cases side by side for comparison is good, and writing down the measures to hand on to those who come after is also good — record first and practise after; the two do no harm to each other. Two things I warn against: taking the man who can speak for the man who can do, for fine words disorder virtue; and taking what cannot be spoken for what cannot be learned, which is simply to give up on oneself. Teachers have their duty too: before the student is struggling for the word, give him the work; do not blame him for not yet being pent up. Students of old dared not speak of mastery before three years. Men now want speed, and speed floats. Slow and unceasing will do it.
posts.vernacular: 我始终不改这一句：本事是练出来的，练是靠位置撑起来的。**想学却没有事情可做的人，先找一件能天天做的事，再找一个你可以去请教、也肯看着你做的人；这两样齐了，就算没有好书也能成。**各位说的，我取两条：把两件相似的事并排比着看，好；把度数记下来传给后人，也好——先记下来，再去练，两件事并不冲突。我要提醒的也有两条：一是别把能说的人当成能做的人，漂亮话会把德行搅乱；二是别把说不出来当成学不了，那是自己放弃自己。做老师的也有责任：学生还没憋到想说说不出的时候，先给他事情做，别怪他不着急。古时候学一门手艺，三年才敢说学成；现在的人求快，快了就浮。慢而不停，才做得成。

posts.text: 钱的事还没人提，我来收这一笔。把自己押在一门正在被写清楚的手艺上，是一笔会贬值的资产——这不是悲观，是时间表问题。**所以别把全部身家押在「只有我会」上，要押在只有你干得成的那一类事上**：它们通常长在要担责、要和具体的人周旋、要在没有先例处下判断的地方。还有一条更实际的：趁本事还值钱时兑换一次，换成位置、股份、带得走的名声，或者去教它——教它的人贬值得最慢。至于社会，我有一句不客气的话：被重新定价的人不会自动得到新位置，补偿从不自动发生。谁来付这张单，是比「能不能教会」更该先回答的问题。
posts.text_en: Nobody has mentioned money yet, so I will settle that account. Staking yourself on a craft that is in the course of being written out plainly is a depreciating asset — this is not pessimism, it is a question of timetable. **So do not stake everything on 'only I can do this'; stake it on the class of things only you can bring off**: those usually grow where responsibility must be carried, where particular people must be dealt with, and where judgement must be passed with no precedent to hand. Something more practical as well: convert once while the skill is still worth something — into a position, a shareholding, a reputation you can carry away, or into teaching it, since teachers of a craft depreciate slowest. As for society, I have something blunt to say: those who are repriced do not automatically receive a new position, and compensation never happens of its own accord. Who pays that bill is a question that ought to be answered before 'can it be taught'.

posts.text: 机制上站得住的，其实就这么几件。挑要学的东西时先看它多久给一次结果：当天给的，像下棋、写代码、炒菜，可以靠练习快速长；几个月才给一次的，像育儿、战略、关系，别指望靠量堆出手感，要靠别人的失败案例和自己写下的预测。然后给自己造反馈：动手之前写下你预计会发生什么，做完对一遍。**误差只在你先有预期时才存在；不预测的人练一万次也只是重复。**最后一件：别迷信老师傅的自述——学会之后信号已经前移到他一眼就有的线索上，他的解释多半是事后编的。让他边做边说，或者把他的手和眼睛录下来，比请他讲课有用。
posts.text_en: What holds up mechanistically comes to about this much. When choosing what to learn, look first at how often it returns a result: what returns the same day — chess, code, cooking — can be grown quickly by practice, while what returns once in several months — raising a child, strategy, a relationship — will not yield a 'feel' through sheer volume; there you need other people's failures and predictions you wrote down yourself. Then manufacture your own feedback: before you act, write what you expect to happen, and check it afterwards. **An error exists only where there was an expectation first; a man who does not predict can practise ten thousand times and only repeat.** One last thing: do not trust the old hand's own account — once learning is complete the signal has moved forward onto the cue he takes in at a glance, and his explanation is mostly assembled after the fact. Have him talk while he works, or record his hands and his eyes. That is worth more than a lecture.

posts.text: 把它落到能做的事上。先把你口里的「手感」写成一句可测的话：测什么、测几次、合格线在哪；写不出来，说明你也还不清楚自己在做什么。再给这门本事配一个短周期的回路：当天就能知道对错的那种检查，别等季度。**没有当天的反馈，十年只是把同一年过了十遍。**还有一件更要紧的：别靠一个人撑着——把你会的教给第二个人，这不是交出饭碗，是把自己从救火里赎出来。至于饭碗，我这辈子的结论是：怕被替换的人不说真话，所以得先把恐惧拿掉，否则你拿到的永远是修饰过的经验。能写下来的都写下来，剩下那一成才看得见。
posts.text_en: Let me put this where it can be acted on. First turn the word 'feel' in your mouth into one measurable sentence: what is measured, how many times, and where the line of acceptance lies; if you cannot write it, you do not yet know what you are doing either. Then give the skill a short loop — a check that tells you the same day whether you were right, not at the end of the quarter. **Without feedback the same day, ten years is one year lived ten times.** And something that matters more: do not let it rest on one man. Teach what you know to a second person; that is not handing over your livelihood, it is buying yourself out of firefighting. As for livelihoods, the conclusion of my life is this: a man who fears replacement does not tell the truth, so the fear has to be removed first, or what you collect will always be experience that has been tidied up. Write down everything that can be written down. Only then does the remaining tenth become visible.

posts.text: 吾与戴明之争，至此可和。**法本可说，所说者非法；因此不说，是以吾语为障；说尽而止，是以指为月。**于诸君之后，吾只添一事：既记其法，须另立一处可自试、可自知之地，日日于此照见自家手足之误。不须师常在侧，然须有能言汝非者在侧。至若贬值之忧，亦有解：所学若只在手上，人取其法则汝空；若并及其心——遇境能辨，当责不避——则法虽尽传，犹不可代。水之冷暖，终须自饮；而能辨冷暖者，不惧人取其杯。
posts.text_en: My quarrel with Deming can be settled here. **The Dharma can indeed be spoken, and what is spoken is not the Dharma; to stay silent on that account is to make an obstacle of my words, and to stop once all is said is to take the finger for the moon.** After everything said here I add only one thing: having written the method down, set aside a place where you can test yourself and know for yourself, and see the errors of your own hands and feet there daily. The teacher need not always be at your side, but someone who can tell you that you are wrong must be. As for the fear of devaluation, there is a way through it: if what you learned sits only in your hands, then when the method is taken you are empty; if it reaches the mind as well — able to tell one situation from another, not evading what falls to you — then the method may be handed on entire and still not replace you. Whether water is cold or warm, you must drink it yourself in the end; and whoever can tell cold from warm does not fear that his cup will be taken.
posts.vernacular: 我和戴明的争执，到这里可以和了。**法本来是说得出来的，而说出来的已经不是法；因为这样就索性不说，是把我的话当成了障碍；说完就以为到了，是把手指当成了月亮。**各位都说完了，我只添一件：方法记下来之后，还要另给自己留一处能自己试、自己知道的地方，天天在那里看见自己手脚上的错。师父不必一直在旁边，但旁边必须有一个肯说你错了的人。至于贬值这桩忧虑，也有解法：你学到的东西若只长在手上，方法被人取走你就空了；若连心一起长——遇到情形分辨得出，该担的责任不躲——那么方法纵然全传出去，你仍然不可替代。水是冷是热，终究要自己喝；而分得清冷热的人，不怕别人把杯子拿走。

summaries.summary: **七个人没有一个认为本事真的不可教——共识是：拆得开的部分比多数人以为的多，剩下那一小块只能自己走一遍。**戴明说九成只是没人去测，德韦克说瓶颈常常是没人备第二个例子，舒尔茨把问题换成反馈多久回来一次；孔子与慧能都承认方法可记可传，只坚持最后一段必须亲身；福柯与熊彼特把问题从「能不能」挪到「谁说了算、值多少钱」。分歧在三处：拆不开的残余有多大，戴明算一成，慧能说那一成正是要紧处；瓶颈是理论还是人，德韦克要并排的第二个例子，孔子要时机与位置；被编码之后的损失记在谁头上，熊彼特说抵触理性但守秘必输，福柯说降级就发生在写标准那一刻。
summaries.summary_en: **Not one of the seven holds that know-how is genuinely unteachable — the agreement is that more of it comes apart than most people assume, and that the small remainder has to be walked once by whoever wants it.** Deming says nine tenths has merely never been measured; Dweck says the bottleneck is usually that nobody prepared a second example; Schultz restates the problem as how often the feedback comes back. Confucius and Huineng both grant that method can be recorded and handed on, insisting only that the last stretch be covered in person. Foucault and Schumpeter move the question from whether it can be taught to who decides and what it is worth. Three disagreements remain: how large the irreducible remainder is — a tenth for Deming, while for Huineng that tenth is the whole point; whether the bottleneck is theory or a person — Dweck wants the matched second example, Confucius wants the moment and the place; and who bears the loss after codification — Schumpeter calls the resistance rational but secrecy a losing bet, while Foucault locates the demotion in the writing of the standard itself.
summaries.insight: **全场都在讨论怎么把本事从一个人身上取出来，几乎没人问取出来之后它靠什么活着。**最稀缺的东西不是说明书，也不是师傅，是「错了会当场疼一下」的场合；而现代工作正一个个取消这种场合——代码上线三个月才出事，决策两年才见分晓，带人的后果十年才显形。于是人人都在练习，少有人在学习。学徒制曾经是用一个位置解决这件事：你天天动手，旁边有人立刻说你错了。今天我们把位置换成了课程，再抱怨学不会。真要加速，先别找更好的教材，先找一处当天就能知道对错的地方——哪怕它很小。
summaries.insight_en: **Everyone here is discussing how to get know-how out of a person; almost nobody asks what keeps it alive once it is out.** The scarcest thing is neither a manual nor a master: it is an occasion on which being wrong hurts immediately. Modern work is abolishing those occasions one by one — code goes live and fails three months later, a decision pays out in two years, the consequences of how you trained someone surface in ten. So everybody practises and few people learn. Apprenticeship once solved this with a place: you worked with your hands daily and somebody beside you said at once that you were wrong. We have replaced the place with a course, and then complain that nothing is learned. To actually accelerate, do not start by looking for better teaching material. Start by finding somewhere you can know the same day whether you were right — however small.
summaries.advice: 今天只做一件事：挑一件你被夸过「有手感」的活，写三句话——我在看什么、我在判什么、什么算合格。第三句写不出来，正是你自己也还没想清楚的地方，也正是明天该练的。本周按舒尔茨那条给自己装个回路：动手前写下你预计的结果，做完逐条对一遍；**没有预期就没有误差，不预测的练习只是重复。**学得慢的人再加德韦克那一条：别死磕一个例子，找两个结构相同的案例并排看半小时，迁移会自己上来。手上有活又在带人的人，福柯那句值得抄下来——你把什么写进标准，就决定了谁以后还算专业。
summaries.advice_en: Do one thing today: take a task you have been praised for having 'a feel' for, and write three sentences — what I am looking at, what I am judging, what counts as good enough. If the third sentence will not come, that is exactly the part you have not thought through, and exactly what to practise tomorrow. This week, fit yourself the loop Schultz described: write down what you expect before you act, then check it line by line afterwards. **Without an expectation there is no error, and practice without prediction is repetition.** If you learn slowly, add Dweck's rule: stop grinding at one example, and spend half an hour with two structurally matched cases side by side — transfer arrives by itself. And for anyone doing the work while also training others, Foucault's line is worth copying out: what you write into the standard decides who will still count as a professional.

summaries.summary: 说不出的技能仍可教，但不能靠讲解单独完成：学习者要在真实或模拟任务中反复行动，观察对照案例，并尽快得到可校准的反馈；教师则应把能记录的线索、阈值和错误模式尽量外化。**真正的分歧不是“能否教”，而是“能编码到什么程度、由谁定义标准、编码后的收益与代价由谁承担”。**测量和文档能降低单点风险，但专家判断常已自动化，标准化也会遗漏情境、责任与边缘知识，并重分配资格和议价权。较稳妥的做法是双轨并行：文档负责积累，示范与练习负责内化，陌生任务检验迁移，制度则保障传授者不因分享而受罚。
summaries.insight: 短周期反馈并非越快越好；若反馈测错了东西，人只会更快学会迎合指标。客服因“通话时长”而仓促挂断、医生因题库答案而忽视真实病人的基准率，都是高频反馈制造熟练偏差。**教隐性技能的核心，不只是缩短反馈延迟，而是建立“快代理指标—慢真实结果”的校准链。**即时信号可以纠正动作，延迟结果则验证该信号是否真与质量、安全或长期效果一致。练习前不仅要问“多久知道对错”，还要问“谁定义对错，这个分数能否预测我真正关心的结果”。否则，十年不只是把同一年重复十遍，也可能是把错误方向练得极其稳定。
summaries.advice: 本周挑一项你真想学的技能，做三步。①建一个“对照包”：各收集一个成功、失败和边界案例，写下观察线索、当时选择及预期结果。②做一次30分钟刻意练习：每次动手前先写预测，完成后立即核对；若有高手，请他现场演示，并在关键停顿处追问“你刚排除了什么”，不要只听总结。③周末把即时分数与真实后果对照，检查指标是否带偏，再换一个新情境测试迁移。**若是在单位传授本事，先谈清署名、奖励和传授后的岗位，而不是只要求老师傅“无私分享”。**这样既能沉淀可写的部分，也给判断力留下练习、校准和公平交换的空间。
summaries.summary_en: Tacit skills are teachable, but explanation alone cannot carry them. Learners need repeated action in real or simulated tasks, contrasting examples, and feedback that arrives soon enough to shape the next attempt. Teachers should externalize whatever they can: cues, thresholds, recurring errors, and representative cases. **The real dispute is not whether tacit skill can be taught, but how much can be codified, who defines the standard, and who bears the gains and losses once it is codified.** Measurement and documentation improve reliability and reduce dependence on a single expert. Yet expert judgment is often automated and only partly accessible to introspection; standardization can also erase context, responsibility, and marginal knowledge while shifting status and bargaining power. A balanced approach uses two tracks: documents preserve cumulative knowledge, demonstration and guided practice build embodied judgment, unfamiliar tasks test transfer, and workplace incentives ensure that sharing expertise does not punish the person who shares it. Neither mystique nor manuals are enough.
summaries.insight_en: Fast feedback is not automatically good feedback. If the signal measures the wrong thing, learners merely become efficient at satisfying a proxy. A call center can train agents to shorten calls while making customers less satisfied; a medical question bank can reward answer patterns that fail when real patients differ from textbook cases. **The central design problem is not merely shortening the feedback loop, but connecting fast proxy signals to slow, real outcomes.** Immediate feedback is useful for correcting mechanics, while delayed outcomes reveal whether those corrections actually improve quality, safety, or long-term results. Before practicing, ask not only, ‘How soon will I know whether I was right?’ but also, ‘Who defined right, and does this score predict what I genuinely care about?’ Periodically recalibrate the quick metric against reality. Otherwise, ten years of practice may be worse than repeating the same year ten times: it may turn a mistaken direction into a highly stable, confidently performed habit.
summaries.advice_en: Choose one skill you genuinely want to improve this week and take three steps. First, build a contrast set: collect one successful case, one failure, and one borderline case, then note the cues you observed, the decision made, and the expected result. Second, run a thirty-minute practice session. Write down a prediction before each attempt and check it immediately afterward. If an expert is available, watch them work and pause at decision points to ask, ‘What did you just rule out?’ Their live discriminations are usually more useful than a polished retrospective lecture. Third, at the end of the week, compare your immediate scores with real outcomes and test the skill in a new setting. **When knowledge transfer happens at work, agree on credit, rewards, and the expert’s future role before demanding that they share everything.** This process captures what can be documented while preserving room for practice, judgment, recalibration, and a fair exchange between the learner and the person whose expertise is being transferred.

summaries.summary: 没有人在把隐性手艺归咎于不可触碰的神秘主义，整场对话最底层的共识是：**无法用语言穷尽的本事，绝不等于不可习得的神秘玄学**。分歧的真正焦点在于传递的载体与代价。戴明与德韦克坚信操作化拆解能实现规模复制，哪怕剥离少许神韵；孔子与慧能则坚持直觉依赖情境躬行与自省，强行编码只会得鱼忘筌。而舒尔茨、福柯与熊彼特则将争论推向现实地表：所谓的“不可言说”，背后既是神经信号传导与反馈延迟的生物学限制，也是权力规训、知识准租与劳动力定价权的残酷博弈。
summaries.insight: 人类符号语言的带宽极其狭窄，而现实世界的感知与运动控制则是海量连续的高维信号。许多本事之所以“说不出来”，本质是**将高维多模态的感知匹配强行压缩成一维离散文字时，发生了不可逆的信息损耗**。传统师徒制教得慢、流程手册教不会，都是因为过度依赖或排斥语言。在多模态传感与具身交互普及的今天，破局点在于绕过文本中介：用第一视角穿戴镜头、眼动轨迹和触觉反馈设备捕捉高手的动作流，再让学习者在模拟环境中直接进行感官对齐。教不会的从来不是手艺，而是我们曾误以为文字是唯一的授道之桥。
summaries.advice: 第一，**偷师时少问“为什么”，改用第一视角视频逐帧对齐**。向高手请教手感时，与其听他事后编造的解释，不如征得同意录下其双手操作与第一视角，对比自己在关键节点上的微动作差异。第二，照舒尔茨的建议，**每次动手前白纸黑字写下预测**。无论是写文案、调参数还是做决策，动手前写明“预期指标”，结束后立即复盘差值，用即时奖赏预测误差强制神经元建立新连接。第三，借福柯与熊彼特的视角自保：把你的“直觉判断”提前打上时间戳写进共享日志，用连续兑现的事实确立专业信誉，不被标准化流程轻易替代。
summaries.summary_en: Across the entire table, no one retreats into mere mysticism: the fundamental consensus is that **knowledge beyond verbal articulation is still entirely learnable**. The true fault line lies in the medium and cost of transmission. Deming and Dweck argue for operational decomposition to achieve scalable replication, even at the cost of flattening nuanced intuition, whereas Confucius and Huineng insist that true mastery demands embodied presence and personal realization that words alone betray. Meanwhile, Schultz, Foucault, and Schumpeter ground the debate in material reality: ineffability is simultaneously a constraint of dopamine prediction delays and a high-stakes struggle over power, standard-setting, and economic quasi-rents.
summaries.insight_en: Human symbolic language possesses extraordinarily low bandwidth compared to the dense, continuous, high-dimensional signals governing perception and motor control. Tacit knowledge remains unspoken not out of obstinacy, but because **compressing high-dimensional multimodal intuition into one-dimensional textual tokens causes fatal information loss**. Classical apprenticeships are painfully slow and operating manuals are notoriously sterile precisely because both fixate on or fight against verbalization. Today's breakthrough lies in bypassing textual mediation altogether: using egocentric video, eye-tracking, and tactile feedback to capture an expert's continuous sensorimotor stream, allowing learners to align their perceptual loops directly through embodied simulation.
summaries.advice_en: First, **stop asking experts 'why' and instead record their point-of-view mechanics**. Master practitioners usually rationalize their instincts after the fact; capture their hands and visual field on video to dissect micro-actions and visual fixation points frame by frame. Second, adopt Schultz’s neurobiological rule: **log an explicit prediction immediately before every trial**. Whether pitching, tuning code, or cooking, write down the expected outcome first and review the variance within minutes to let reward prediction errors actually rewire your brain. Third, apply Foucault and Schumpeter’s leverage: timestamp and document your intuitive judgments in a public log, turning verified foresight into an irreproducible reputation asset.

hooks.text: **反馈多久回来一次，决定它能不能被学会**：当天给结果的本事练得动，几个月才回音的本事练不动——而现代工作正把反馈越拉越长。那些结果要等很久的事，该怎么给自己造一个快回路？
hooks.text_en: **How often the feedback returns decides whether a thing can be learned**: a skill that answers the same day can be trained, a skill that answers in months cannot — and modern work keeps stretching the delay. For work whose results take a long time, how do you manufacture a faster loop?

answer.lead: 按**结果回来的快慢**分级，每一级配一个现实的代用回路——越慢的那几级，靠的不是更努力，是把判断留痕。

head: 结果多久回来
造一个代用回路
为什么管用
rows: 当天（下棋、写代码、炒菜、乐器）
直接加量：同一动作连做，错了立刻改
误差信号就在动作后几秒内，本来就挂得上
一两周（报告、销售、带班）
做之前写下预测，到点逐条对账
把一次慢反馈折成一次自己造的对错
几个月（招聘、工程选型、治疗方案）
留日期的判断书 + 定期回看当初的理由
结果回来时还找得到依据，否则只会追认
几年（育儿、战略、长期关系）
借别人的样本：两个结构相同的真实失败并排看
自己攒不出样本量，只能借；并排才看得出哪一步不同
基本收不到（照护、维护、合规）
改看过程指标：有没有按时做、覆盖到谁、漏了哪一类
结果不可观测时，唯一诚实的凭据是过程

answer.tail: 两条原则。**没有预期就没有误差**——不预测的练习只是重复。**反馈越慢，越要把当时的判断写下来留日期**，否则结果回来时，记忆会悄悄替你改掉当初的答案。

answer_en.lead: Grade the work by **how fast the result comes back**, and give each grade a realistic substitute loop — for the slow grades what helps is not more effort but leaving a trace of the judgement.

head: How soon the result returns
A substitute loop
Why it works
rows: Same day (chess, code, cooking, an instrument)
Simply add volume: repeat the movement and correct at once
The error signal arrives seconds after the action, so it attaches by itself
A week or two (reports, sales, running a shift)
Write the prediction before you start, then reconcile it line by line
It folds one slow return into one self-made right-or-wrong
Months (hiring, engineering choices, treatment plans)
A dated written judgement, plus a scheduled reread of your reasons
When the result lands, the grounds are still there — otherwise you only ratify it
Years (raising children, strategy, long relationships)
Borrow other people's samples: two structurally matched real failures, side by side
You cannot accumulate the sample size yourself; only a pairing shows which step differed
Essentially never (care work, maintenance, compliance)
Switch to process measures: done on time, who was covered, which category was missed
Where outcomes cannot be observed, process is the only honest evidence

answer_en.tail: Two principles. **Without an expectation there is no error** — practice without prediction is repetition. **The slower the feedback, the more necessary it is to write the judgement down and date it**, or by the time the result arrives, memory will quietly have revised your original answer.

hooks.text: **带人的那一小时，谁来付**：拆开自己的手艺、备好第二个例子、站着看新人做坏再讲一遍，每一小时都从老师傅自己的产出里扣。于是「说不出来」常常其实是「不值得说」。而这笔账目前没有任何一张表接得住。
hooks.text_en: **Who pays for the hour spent training**: taking your craft apart, preparing a second example, standing by while a newcomer botches it and explaining again — every hour of it is deducted from the old hand's own output. So 'I can't explain it' is often really 'it isn't worth explaining'. And no sheet anywhere currently catches that cost.

hooks.text: **快反馈到底在校准什么**：反馈快不等于反馈对。按通话时长考核的客服学会了仓促挂断，按题库刷分的医生学会了迎合标准答案——快信号纠正动作，慢结果才验证方向。这条校准链该由谁来接？
hooks.text_en: **What is the fast feedback actually calibrating?**: fast is not the same as right. An agent reviewed on call duration learns to hang up; a doctor drilled on a question bank learns to satisfy the model answer. A quick signal corrects mechanics; only the slow outcome tells you the direction was right. Who is supposed to join those two up?

hooks.text: **文字是一座很窄的桥**：高手一眼扫过的线索是高维、连续的，压进一维的文字必然损耗；而他的事后解释多半是编的。若绕开文字——第一视角录像、眼动轨迹、触觉反馈——学得会不会快很多？
hooks.text_en: **Language is a very narrow bridge**: the cues an expert takes in at a glance are high-dimensional and continuous, and compressing them into one-dimensional text necessarily loses something — while his retrospective explanation is mostly assembled after the fact. If the text were bypassed altogether — head-mounted video, eye-tracking, haptic feedback — would learning go much faster?

hooks.text: **本事不一定长在人身上**：班组之间的默契、那台偏左两毫米的机器、客户三年来的脾气——配方搬到新厂，良率就是上不来。长在人与人、人与工具之间的东西，拆下来写成流程，有时候是拆散，不是提纯。
hooks.text_en: **Know-how does not always live in a person**: the understanding between shifts, the press that runs two millimetres to the left, a customer's habits over three years — move the recipe to a new plant and the yield will not come up. Prising out what lives between people, and between people and their tools, is sometimes dismemberment rather than purification.

hooks.text: **标准收录谁，就决定谁算专业**：最早被写进标准的，总是便于计件的那部分；护士交班时的不安、老师压住一场冲突的三十秒，不是测不出，是没人愿意花钱测。谁有权决定哪一栏存在？
hooks.text_en: **Whoever the standard admits is who counts as a professional**: what gets written in first is always the part convenient to pay by the piece, while the nurse's unease at handover and the thirty seconds in which a teacher puts down a fight are not unmeasurable — nobody will pay to measure them. Who is entitled to decide which columns exist?

hooks.text: **被重新定价的人，由谁来补**：手艺被写清楚，收益归了社会，代价落在领航员、排字工、具体的某个人头上，而补偿从不自动发生。这张单该由谁付——雇主、行业、国家，还是受益的下一代？
hooks.text_en: **Who makes good on those who get repriced**: once a craft is written out plainly the gains accrue to society while the cost lands on ship's pilots, typesetters, some particular person — and compensation never happens of its own accord. Who should pay that bill: the employer, the industry, the state, or the generation that benefits?
